thread:
nina (sec): Heads-up: Received DSAR from user requesting full account delete (acct: demo-guest-88). They want deletion, a signed proof, and confirmation that any KMS-wrapped backups are unrecoverable.

omar (privacy): Do we know where embeddings live (managed vector service vs external vendor)? Also check retention-exception flags before starting.

nina (sec): Embeddings in our internal vector-store + snapshot copies in s3 and in cold archive. No external vendors. Retention-service shows a potential ticket flagged last month but no legal hold.

ash (infra): KMS detail: snapshots are encrypted with our managed keystore key id rk-2345. Cold archive uses envelope encryption with wrapping key. If customer wants unrecoverability we need to show key rotation or destruction events. We can't share material keys.

rebecca (legal): For the proof: include scope, object ids, deletion timestamps, acting principal (role ARN), and signed digest of manifest. We'll review wording.

ops-bot: Retention-service: account demo-guest-88 -> retention_flag: none. Active holds: 0.

omar (privacy): Proposed safe flow: 1) Lock account writes 2) Create short-lived dsar-erasure role 3) Snapshot object-list export 4) Execute targeted erase on vector index + delete snapshot objects 5) Rotate managed keystore wrapping key + record rotation event 6) Verification queries and audit bundle generation 7) Legal review before release.

nina (sec): Agree. Need RBAC control: dsar-erasure role should be ephemeral, scope-limited to resource tags (acct:demo-guest-88), MFA enforced, and only creatable by sec/priv team.

ash (infra): I'll add an IAM guard for resource-based condition "redwood:account == demo-guest-88" and TTL 3h. Command: `tools/iam/temp-grant --role dsar-erasure --resource-tag account=demo-guest-88 --ttl 3h --mfa`. Will log role ARN to infra audit.

kms-bot: KMS log snapshot: key rk-2345 versions: v1,v2. Last rotate: 2026-01-15T12:02:18Z. Decrypt attempts: none in last 90d.

omar (privacy): Important: deleting objects doesn't strictly prevent future decrypt if key material persists. For managed keys we can rotate and then mark previous versions revoked — include rotation digest in proof. For customer-managed keys advise them to rotate and destroy if they require cryptographic irrecoverability.

rebecca (legal): We'll need a cover note clarifying the limits of our attestation. Also include a signed manifest hash and the identity that ran erasure. No raw key material in bundle.

nina (sec): Practical verification: after erase job, run `vector-find --account demo-guest-88 --hashes <exported-fingerprints>` -> expect 0 results. Also check s3 object-list shows delete markers and object deletion receipts.

ash (infra): Implementation plan: 1) export object ids: `privacy-tools export-objects --acct demo-guest-88 --out ids.json` 2) run erasure: `kubectl -n privacy run erasure --image=privacy/eraser:stable -- --input ids.json --confirm` 3) rotate wrapping key: `kms rotate rk-2345 --note dsar-demo-guest-88` 4) gather logs: S3 deletion receipts, kube job logs, kms rotation event, iam role usage -> bundle.

ops-bot: Note: If vulnerability or incident is open for the account, escalation required per vuln-triage policy. Check SecurityIncidentManager.

omar (privacy): I checked SIM: no active incidents. Good to proceed.

rebecca (legal): Also ask requester whether they need a certified/legalized proof (notarized). That changes process and timeline.

nina (sec): Timeline estimate: 3-8 hours (no holds, no cross-region replication), add extra time if archive retrieval needed. I'll reply to requester.

ash (infra): One more: post-erasure we should rotate any service principals that had read access to these buckets to reduce accidental restores. I'll add service principal rotation to the playbook.

omar (privacy): Data minimization note: let's ensure future TTL set for demo accounts = 30d by default. I'll file a follow-up ticket for product.

nina (sec): Action list: 1) ash creates dsar-erasure ephemeral role + post ARN 2) omar prepare object export + run erasure-run 3) ash rotate rk-2345 and collect KMS rotation event 4) omar+nina run verification queries 5) rebecca draft cover note. Post proof bundle here and legal will review.

ash (infra): Creating role now. Will post ARN and audit link.

ops-bot: IAM: temporary role dsar-erasure created arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/dsar-erasure-demo-guest-88 (expires 2026-03-21T18:14:32Z). Audit link: https://infra.redwood/audit/roles/4332

nina (sec): Good. Omar, when you have ids.json paste checksum here so we can sign manifest.

omar (privacy): ids.json exported: checksum sha256: 6b2e9a1f4c8e2b9fd2d8b5a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3

ash (infra): Erasure job started: job-id erasure-20260321-07. I'll stream logs to the audit link.

ops-bot: Job update: erasure-20260321-07 -> 50% (deleting vector shards).

nina (sec): Reminder: capture who executed the job (principal) and include tty recording for interactive steps.

kms-bot: Rotate command complete. rk-2345 new version v3 created. Rotation event id rot-9988 timestamp 2026-03-21T17:45:12Z.

omar (privacy): Erasure finished. Verification: `vector-find` returned 0 hits for exported fingerprints. S3 delete markers present for snapshot objects. Generated manifest.json and signed_digest: sha256: abcd1234ef567890...

rebecca (legal): I'll draft the cover letter and review manifest. Please attach the audit bundle link when ready.

nina (sec): Posting audit bundle: https://infra.redwood/audit/bundles/erasure-4332 (includes kube logs, s3 receipts, kms rotation, iam usage).

rebecca (legal): Reviewed. Adding standard legal clauses and preparing to send. If requester asks for notarized proof escalate to legal ops.

nina (sec): Closing loop: reply to requester giving timeline, proof bundle availability, and caveats about cryptographic irrecoverability for customer-managed keys. Marking thread closed after send. :white_check_mark:
